description: Preview how a public Sequenzy email gallery email would read for this company without saving any email (a company's first AI generation saves its inferred email design direction, like generate_email): the same rewrite as create_template_from_example (the example's layout, every word written for the company, its logo, brand color and links swapped in), returned as subject, previewText and HTML. Pass website to write it for another site's brand instead, such as a prospect or client; it is looked up like the gallery's public preview. Requires templates:write. Takes 5-20 seconds. Call create_template_from_example to keep it as a template. Accepts a gallery email URL or brand plus email slugs.

brand.description: Gallery brand slug from the URL (/email-examples/brands/{brand}/...). Use with the example slug instead of url.

brief.description: Optional direction, up to 1000 characters, such as an offer or feature to highlight. Takes priority over the example.

companyId.description: Company ID. If not provided, uses the currently selected company.

email.description: Gallery email slug from the URL (/emails/{email}). Use with brand instead of url.

url.description: Email gallery page URL. Provide either url, or brand plus the example slug; not both.

website.description: Optional site or domain, like acme.com, to write the preview for instead of this company's own brand.

name: preview_template_from_example

outputSchema.description: Structured content returned by the `preview_template_from_example` MCP tool.

example.description: The gallery example it is modeled on: brand, subject and url.

items.description: Fallback array wrapper used only when a tool returns a bare array.

message.description: That nothing was saved, and how to save it.

preview.description: The unsaved rewrite: brandName and website (whose brand it is written in; website null for this company's own), subject, previewText and html.

value.description: Fallback object wrapper used only when a tool returns a non-object value.

warnings.description: Non-fatal cautions about content, permissions, or follow-up actions.
